findings.title: Recurring calendar deletions are raced against the final cleanup wait
findings.body: The async `forEach` is not awaited. Since each callback now awaits `getCalendar()` before pushing its deletion promise into `apiDeletes`, execution can reach the later `Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` while `apiDeletes` is still empty or incomplete. The cancellation request can therefore finish (and in a serverless worker be terminated) without deleting some recurring events from external calendars, and import/delete failures become unhandled rejections. Build and await a `Promise.all` for these callbacks before relying on `apiDeletes`.

findings.title: Reschedule cleanup launches unobserved async calendar deletions
findings.body: Changing this callback to `async` without replacing `forEach` with an awaited `Promise.all` means the new `await getCalendar()` and the subsequent `deleteEvent()` are detached from `Reschedule`. The surrounding `try/catch` does not catch rejections from async `forEach` callbacks, so a failed dynamic import or external calendar deletion is unhandled while the function continues to send the reschedule email and return success. Await the mapped cleanup operations inside the try block.

findings.title: Request-reschedule returns before asynchronously loaded integrations are deleted
findings.body: The async callback passed to `forEach` is never awaited. With the new asynchronous `getCalendar`, this mutation marks the booking cancelled and sends the reschedule email before the calendar module has necessarily loaded or its event deletion has run; failures are also unhandled. This can leave the old external calendar/video meeting active even though the booking is cancelled. Collect the callback promises with `map` and await `Promise.all` before completing the mutation.
